Definition: a channel (into which water is raised for irrigation); also a bandage or plaster (as placed upon a wound)
BiblicalUsage: The word is a conduit, a channel for water. Elijah built a trench about the altar, as great as would contain two measures of seed, and filled it with water; Hezekiah made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city; and Ezekiel says the waters made the cedar great, and the deep sent out her little rivers unto all the trees of the field.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that water carried by a channel is life carried where it is needed, and Hezekiah's conduit is the picture of a king who provides.
